{{c|{{larger|S. LUKES GOSPEL.}}}}

{{dropinitial|S}}''. LUKES Gospel may be diuided into fiue partes.''

''The first part is, of the Infancie both of the precursor, and of Christ himself: chap. 1 and 2. The second, of the Preparation that was made to the manifestation of Christ: chap. 3 and a piece of the 4.''

''The third, of Christes manifesting himself, by preaching and miracles, specially in Galilee: the other piece of the 4. chap. vnto the middes of the 17.''

''The fourth of his comming into Iurie towards his Passion: the other piece of the 17. chap. vnto the middes of the 19.''

''The fifth, of the Holy Weeke of his Passion in Hierusalem: the other part of the 19. chap. vnto the end of the booke.''

''S. Luke was'' sectator ''(saith S. Hierome)'' that is, a disciple of the Apostle Paul, and a companion of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Hier. in Catalogo.}}al his peregrination''. And the same we see in the Actes of the Apostles: Where, from the 16. chap. S. Luke putteth himself in the traine of S. Paul, writing thus in the storie.'' Forthwith we sought to goe into Macedonia''. And in like maner, in the first person, commonly through the rest of that booke. Of him and his Gospel, S. Hierom vnderstandeth this saying of S. Paul:'' We haue sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the Gospel through al Churches''. Where also he addeth:'' Some suppose, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=2. Cor. 8, 18.}}so often as Paul in his Epistles saith'', According to my Gospel,'' that he meaneth of Lukes booke''. And againe:'' Luke learned the Gospel not onely of the Apostle Paul, who had not been with our Lord in flesh, but of the other Apostles: which himself also in the beginning of his booke declareth, saying, As {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Luk. 1, 2.}}they deliuered to vs who themselves from the beginning saw, and were ministers of the word''. It foloweth in S. Hierome:'' Therfore he wrote the Gospel, as he had heard; but the Actes of the Apostles he compiled as he had seen''. S. Paul writeth of him by name to the Colossians:'' Luke the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Col. 4, 14.}}Physicion saluteth you''. And to Timothee:'' Luke alone is with me''. Finally of his end thus doth S. ''{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=2. Tim. 4, 11.}}''Hierome write:'' He liued fourescore and foure yeres, hauing no wife. He is buried at Constantinople; {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Hiero. in Catalogo.}}to which citie his bones with the Relikes of Andrew the Apostle were translated out of Achaia the twentieth yere of ˹Constantinus˺''. And of the same Translation also in another place against ''{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Constantius.''}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Hier. con. Vigil. c. 2.}}''Vigilantius the Heretike:'' It grieueth him that the Relikes of the Martyrs are couered with pretious couerings, and that they are not either tied in cloutes or throwen to the dunghil. Why, are we then {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Heretike so counted the Catholikes for their honouring of Saincts, and Relikes.}}sacrilegious, when we enter the Churches of the Apostles? Was ˹Constantinus˺ the Emperour {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Constantius.''}}sacrilegious, who translated to Constantinople the holy Relikes of Andrew, Luke, and Timothee: at which the Devil's rore, and the inhabiters of Vigilantius confesse that they feele their presence?

''His sacred body is now at Padua in Italie, wither it was againe translated from Constantinople.''<noinclude>{{rh||R iij|THE}}</noinclude>
